 Maresca makes three changes for Forest trip 
 Rob Pollard 
 @RobPollardMCFC 
 Sat 07 Nov 2026, 16:15 
 Share 
 Enzo Maresca has made three changes from the side that defeated RB Leipzig on Wednesday as City look to get back to winning ways in the Premier League at Nottingham Forest this evening. 
 Men's Team

 Rúben Dias, Joško Gvardiol and Jérémy Doku all come into the starting XI, with Matheus Nunes, Nico O’Reilly and Phil Foden moving to the bench.
 City start the day second in the Premier League, with 21 points from our first nine games of the season. 
 TEAMS
 FOREST: Sels, Murillo, Milenkovic, Jair Cunha, Williams, Schlager, McAtee, Munoz, Yates, Gibbs-White, Delap
 SUBS: John Victor, Diomande, Sangare, Hudson-Odoi, Wood, Igor Jesus, Ndoye, Kalimuendo, Netz
 CITY: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Anderson, Fernández, Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku, Haaland 
 SUBS: Rulli, Kovačić, Reis, Nunes, Bouaddi, O’Reilly, Allan Elias, Foden, Lewis

 Tactics 
 Enzo Maresca’s tactics are often fluid, but it looks like City will start in a 4-2-3-1 formation. 
 Gianluigi Donnarumma starts in goal, with Abdukodir Khusanov at right-back and Joško Gvardiol at left-back. 
 Rúben Dias captains the side and starts alongside Marc Guéhi at centre-half. 
 Elliot Anderson returns to his former club in a defensive midfield role, alongside Enzo Fernández, who will have licence to get forward and support attacks.
 Iliman Ndiaye will play down the right, with Jérémy Doku on the left. 
 And in-form Rayan Cherki will play just off central striker Erling Haaland in attack. 
 Anderson is key
 Elliot Anderson returns to Forest today, the Club he spent two seasons with before joining City this summer. 
 It’s fair to say the 24-year-old has adapted well to new surroundings - he has been sensational so far this season and is arguably City’s most important player right now. 
 A superb engine, great range of passing and wonderful vision - he is a complete midfielder who consistently wins his duels. 
 If City are to get three points today, it’s likely Anderson will be key to the win. 
 ‘A manager’s dream,’ was Enzo Maresca’s pre-match assessment of Anderson. 
  “Knowing him now, no. He’s a guy who wants to learn every day,” Maresca said.
 “We start with him on the video, he wants to understand, learn and improve - which for a manager is a dream because you know he wants to learn and do different things.
 “I don’t remember exactly [the first time I saw him play] but I remember the first conversation with him which was about which position, but again the feeling immediately was very good.
 “You can see how intelligent he is. It’s important.
 “ I knew him from Newcastle where he struggled a little bit, then Forest. And I faced him with Chelsea different times.
 “I know how good he is.”
 Return to winning ways?
 After winning our opening seven matches of the season in fine style, City come into this one on the back of two successive defeats in the Premier League. 
 It has allowed Arsenal, who face Hull City at the Emirates in one of the 15:00 (UK) kick-offs this afternoon, to edge ahead of us at the top of the table.
 It’s early stages and no one at City will be panicking, but given the quality across the Premier League, Maresca will be desperate to get back to winning ways today and reassert our credentials ahead of the international break.

 Match stats 
 Nottingham Forest have won one of their last nine Premier League games against Manchester City (D3 L5), a 1-0 home win in the 2024-25 season. 
 Manchester City are looking to record consecutive away top-flight wins at Nottingham Forest for the first time since January 1925. 
 Nottingham Forest are winless in their last six Premier League home games (D3 L3), failing to score in each of their last four. Only twice have they had a longer run without a home league goal – six games between November 2011/January 2012 and five games between December 2017/February 2018. 
 Nottingham Forest have failed to score in all four of their home league games this season, with three 1-0 defeats and a 0-0 draw. Only three teams in top-flight history have failed to score in their first five of a campaign – West Brom in 1921-22, Everton in 1998-99 and Huddersfield in 2018-19. 
 Having become the 10th team in English top-flight history to win each of their first seven games in a campaign, Man City have now lost their last two. Only Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05 have won their first seven and then lost their next three. 
 Man City have lost their last two Premier League games, as many as they had in their previous 33 (W23 D8). Only once in the last 10 years have they lost more consecutively, losing four in a row in November/December 2024. 
 Despite having the second-most shots in the Premier League this season (152), Nottingham Forest have scored the fewest goals (6). They also have the lowest shot conversion rate (4%) and biggest negative xG difference (-8.3) so far this term. 
 Man City have the highest expected goals total (18.3), and the highest average xG per shot (0.13) of any side in the Premier League this season. 
 Morgan Gibbs-White could make his 200th Premier League appearance in this match. 151 of his 199 so far have been for Nottingham Forest, the third-most for the club in the competition. 
 Man City midfielder Elliot Anderson has made more passes while under high pressure than any other player in the Premier League this season (357).
